title: Files
summary: fopen opens a file and returns a FILE pointer, or NULL with errno saying why. The familiar fprintf, fgets and fscanf work on any FILE, and stdin, stdout and stderr are FILEs too. fwrite and fread move raw bytes, fseek and ftell move around in a file, and every opened file must be closed.

cards.q: What does fopen("log.txt", "w") do to an existing log.txt?
cards.a:
Empties it

Use "a" to add to the end instead.

cards.q: How do you find out why fopen failed?
cards.a:
errno, through perror or strerror

fopen returns NULL and sets errno.

Only 7 items of 4 bytes could be read

The count is in items, not bytes. Fewer than asked usually means the end of the file (or an error, which `ferror` tells apart).

cards.q: Why write errors to stderr instead of stdout?
cards.a:
They stay visible when output is redirected

Results and messages go to different places, so `prog > out.txt` still shows errors on the terminal.
